title: SDK ergonomics starter kits: streaming + retries cookbook for Next.js / FastAPI / Go / CLI
creator: Marcos Rivera
description: Deliver a small collection of idiomatic starter templates and cookbook snippets that show best-practice patterns for: (1) resilient retries with idempotency and backoff across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, (2) ergonomic streaming and cancelation patterns (server-sent events / ReadableStream / chunked responses / http.Flusher), and (3) minimal CLI examples for batch inference / resumable uploads. These artifacts must be small, copy-paste friendly, and instrumented with Redwood SDK telemetry hooks (token counts, latency). Aim for parity across three languages so engineers can reason about behavior consistently.
acceptance_criteria:
1) 4 runnable examples (Next.js streaming page, FastAPI streaming endpoint, Go HTTP server streaming handler, CLI batch + retry) with README usage and expected output.
2) Each example includes a small test script that validates retry/backoff logic and streaming chunk ordering.
3) SDK-level helpers documented (retry decorator/options, stream iterator abstraction, cancellation token) and upstreamed to sdks repo.
4) Code reviewed and security sign-off for any network retry/idempotency semantics.
5) Performance sanity checks: sample trace showing <50ms extra overhead for SDK helpers on a simple echo model.

implementation_plan:
1) Finalize cross-language SDK helpers: retry policy (max_retries, max_elapsed_time, backoff_base, jitter) and stream adapter (async iterator in Python/TS, channel-like iterator in Go).
2) Implement Next.js example (server action -> streaming server component) with ReadableStream and cancellation via AbortController.
3) Implement FastAPI example with StreamingResponse + background prewarm and explicit context cancellation.
4) Implement Go HTTP server using http.Flusher, context.WithTimeout, and a small example client showing graceful shutdown.
5) Implement CLI example that demonstrates batching, idempotency keys, resume token storage, and opt-in verbose logging with redaction.
6) Write README + tests + telemetry traces + open PRs.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for retry helper across edge cases (HTTP 429, network broken pipe, 5xx).
- Integration tests: run each example against a local echo model (dockerized) to assert streaming order, idempotency behavior, and no secret leakage in logs.
- Performance check: measure token accounting overhead and report before/after hook latencies.

notes: Trade-offs considered: keeping helpers tiny vs full-featured. Decided to provide composable primitives rather than monolithic abstractions so different runtimes (edge vs dedicated) can opt in. For streaming retries we recommend 'fail-fast and restart stream' for most apps; advanced resume-by-offset will be a follow-up if customers request.
